lede.purpose: Hero identity, chapter text, Time Shift sentence, Case question, close text.

label.purpose: dt labels, metadata, footers, in ink-3.

data.purpose: Fragment Mono: clocks, coordinates, periods, readout values, codes in figures, lens tally.

data-small.purpose: Fragment Mono 11px: note timestamps, can’t tell lines, Field place labels, lens cursor tag.

shadows.name: paper-halo

shadows.name: scan-glow
shadows.purpose: The lens scan line, for its 0.9s pass only.

motion.name: ease-out
motion.purpose: Entrance curve (GSAP CustomEase 'out'): reveals, link underlines, hover slides, top bar, ticker, lens tag, map arrival.

motion.name: ease-scene
motion.purpose: Change of place (GSAP CustomEase 'scene'): route draw, Case expand, reels, entry rules, notes clip, figure steps, lens scan.

motion.name: lenis
motion.purpose: Inertial scroll; off under reduced motion.

motion.name: field-stage
motion.value: stage 0 name, 1 world, 2 visit; per-dot cubic in-out, lag up to 0.45, banded bow up to 0.275 of the leg
motion.purpose: One crowd of dots moves between its three roles.

motion.name: field-arrival
motion.value: mapIn 1.1s out; route 1.7s scene at 0.3s; name gathers 1.55s at 1.85s; once per session, skipped by scroll or hash
motion.purpose: Map, then route Singapore to New York, then the name.

motion.name: attention-trail
motion.value: 20 samples; heat exp(-d²/5000); nudge 16px; fades after 2.5s still
motion.purpose: Pointer warms letters toward blue and nudges them; the attention trace.

motion.name: terminator
motion.value: subsolar point every 60s; day smoothstep ±0.05; dusk band |cosZ| < 0.06
motion.purpose: Night land dims, dusk turns blue.

motion.name: scene-runway
motion.value: Prologue 160vh; Time Shift 150vh (140vh at 700px); sticky 100svh stage
motion.purpose: Scroll-scrubbed scenes; nothing holds the scroll.

motion.name: odometer
motion.value: hours counted one at a time over progress 0.12 to 0.78; click after 55% of each hour; +1 day at midnight
motion.purpose: Time Shift clock with the Field.

motion.name: reel
motion.value: one full turn, 1.6s, scene, 0.1s stagger per digit
motion.purpose: Time Shift digits without the Field; up for forward, down for back.

motion.name: visit-pour
motion.value: row by row, left to right; dot pitch 6 to 13px (4.2 to 9px phones) so the longest row fills about 85%
motion.purpose: World evaporates into the visit readout.

motion.name: figure-steps
motion.value: autoplay on 55% visibility, 2.4s per step; parts ease 1.4s scene; chosen step 0.9s
motion.purpose: Case figures play their argument in place.

motion.name: case-expand
motion.value: pagereveal; new root clip-path from row outline, 1s scene; old root fade + scale 0.975, 0.38s out; title morph via view-transition-name, 1s
motion.purpose: The clicked row grows into the Case.

motion.name: view-transition
motion.value: group 0.9s scene; old root 0.5s fade; new root 0.9s out from 24px after 0.15s

motion.name: chapter-chars
motion.value: yPercent 110 to 0, 1.3s, stagger 0.03s, out, masked, once at top 82%

motion.name: entry-rule
motion.value: scaleX 0 to 1 from left, 1.2s, scene, once at top 88%

motion.name: lens-scan
motion.value: 1px line, 0.9s scene; outlines fade in 0.35s out as the scan reaches them

narrative.overview:
The site is a printed page that is taking notes on its reader. Daylight paper and near-black ink carry everything that is authored; a single annotation blue carries everything that is observed or live. The contrast between the two layers is the whole idea: the ink says what Kaushik did, the blue says what the page can see of you right now, and what it cannot tell.

On the home page the page has one moving image, the Field: a single crowd of about 16,000 dots that is, in turn, the name, the world and the visit. It draws the world with tonight's real day and night, flies the map between the places of the Journey while the clocks count the hours, and ends as a chart of the reader's own time, stated in its unit. Every word the Field depicts is also real HTML underneath it; the canvas is decoration over the truth, never instead of it. Everywhere else the page stays an editorial layout: one grotesk at extreme scale contrast, hairline rules and flush-left columns on a twelve-column grid, flat surfaces. Motion happens between reading moments; reading text sits in quiet zones the dots thin out behind.

The system rejects the template portfolio: no kicker above the hero, no pill buttons, no cards, no decorative gradients, no glass, no 3D. Real photography in full colour is the only colour besides the blue.
keyCharacteristics: Two-layer colour: ink for the authored record, blue for observation and live state.
One variable grotesk (Switzer) at extreme scale contrast; one mono (Fragment Mono) for data only.
One dot field (raw WebGL2, home only) that plays name, world and visit; truth stays in HTML.
Hairline rules instead of containers; square corners throughout.
Two curves for every movement: `out` for entrances, `scene` for changes of place.
Light and dark themes with identical structure; dark follows `prefers-color-scheme` or `[data-theme]`, and the Field reads its colours from the same tokens.

rules.name: The Two Layers Rule
rules.body: Blue means "observed or live". If an element is authored content, it is ink, however important it is. A blue heading, blue button or blue decorative accent breaks the meaning of every note on the page.

rules.name: The Photography Exception Rule
rules.body: Real photographs and real product screenshots keep their full colour. No other colour enters the palette, including inside the Field, which draws only in `ink` and `note`.

rules.name: The Tracking Floor Rule
rules.body: Letter-spacing never goes below -0.04em, at any size.

rules.name: The Six Rem Rule
rules.body: Display type caps at 6rem. Only pinned, one-per-screen elements may exceed it: the hero name, Chapter titles and the Time Shift clocks.

rules.name: The Mono Means Data Rule
rules.body: Fragment Mono is for clocks, coordinates, periods, timestamps, measured values, tags and codes. Never for headings, prose or decoration. The top-bar clock and the large Time Shift digits are Switzer with tabular numerals, because they are read as display, not logged.

rules.name: The Hairline Rule
rules.body: Separation is a 1px line in `rule`, or `ink` when it opens a section. Nothing else divides content.

rules.name: The Clearance Not Lift Rule
rules.body: A shadow exists only to clear text from the Field (in paper) or to mark the lens scan (in blue). No surface ever floats.

rules.name: The Three Properties Rule
rules.body: In the DOM, animate position, opacity and clip only, plus left-origin scaleX for rules and bars. Colour changes only as state (a figure step becoming current) or as the attention trace. Scale appears only for something stepping back or arriving (the old page at 0.975, the lens tag from 0.92).

rules.name: The Welcome Rule
rules.body: The Field runs only on the home page, with WebGL2, and without a reduced-motion preference; the layout class is set before first paint so scroll positions stay stable. If the context is lost, the page falls back to the plain layout: HTML name, static bands, no scenes.

rules.name: The Reduced Motion Rule
rules.body: Under `prefers-reduced-motion: reduce`, the Field never loads, scenes are static bands, figure steps read top to bottom, the view transition is off, reels land on the destination time, reveals and figures show their end state, the lens skips its scan, and Lenis does not run.

dos: **Do** keep annotation blue for notes, live data (clocks, readout values, the unit sentence), the lens, the Field's live marks (dusk, route, traveller, active place, heat), selection and focus.
**Do** separate content with 1px hairlines in `rule`, or `ink` to open a section.
**Do** end every text action with the drawn Arrow in its direction of travel.
**Do** use Fragment Mono only for clocks, coordinates, periods, timestamps, measured values, tags and codes.
**Do** use `out` for entrances and `scene` for changes of place, and nothing else.
**Do** mark reading text that can sit over the Field with `data-quiet`, and give it a paper halo.
**Do** keep every word the Field depicts in real HTML, and state the unit of any dot count.
**Do** tag every new control with `data-observe`, a label and a "can't tell" line.
**Do** give every live or animated element a reduced-motion and no-script end state.
donts: **Don't** set display type above 6rem unless it is the hero name, a Chapter title or a Time Shift clock.
**Don't** add a kicker or eyebrow above any heading.
**Don't** use cards, decorative gradients, glass, drop shadows, pill buttons or 3D.
**Don't** use blue for authored content, headings or decoration.
**Don't** gate identity text behind the arrival, or put the canvas in the accessibility tree.
**Don't** load the Field outside the home page, without WebGL2 or under reduced motion.
**Don't** hold the scroll: scenes are sticky runways, never scroll-jacking.
**Don't** use text glyphs (→) as icons; use the Arrow component.
